question: Does the nominal accuracy/noise tradeoff buy useful large-signal linearity, and how much capacitive-load bandwidth, settling and external source/sink capability is required?
amplitude_scope: Two explicitly changed signal functions. Retain 2-percent THD, 10-percent fundamental gain and .25..75-V output limits. Original 5-mV results/definitions are unchanged. No Local dynamic population claim.
capacitance_basis: The actual roughly 17-kohm output resistance predicts a bandwidth boundary near 9 pF. Choose 8 pF below and 16 pF above it, plus .2 pF to inspect the light-load response. R75 may exceed the old 100-MHz sweep at .2 pF, so these three load sweeps are declared up to 1 GHz before observation.

step.target_method: Separate stationary OP solves at both input endpoints. No tail fitting, rebias or recentering.
step.observed_current: Zero-V series capacitor sensor and every MOS terminal current; output KCL and integral of capacitor current versus C*delta_V. Report actual input/supply delivery and absorption ranges.

refinement.acceptance: Center <1 uV; gain/THD/bandwidth relative change <0.005. Step settling brackets must agree within max(4 ns, 0.005 of time). Retain any discrepancy for bounded diagnosis.

analytic_control.circuit: MOS-free known feedback passive network: Rsrc1k+Rin9k, Rf100k, Rload100k, Cload8p; same input ramp pair and series capacitor sensor.
analytic_control.reason: Check the changed capacitor-current and finite-ramp history extraction before MOS dynamic attempts.

stopping: Exactly these 33 native attempts once at one worker. Stop on unusable numerics or analytic-control failure for bounded diagnosis. Retain physical failures and unsupported domains; no outcome-driven matrix extension. These are known nominal physical inputs, not fresh confirmation.
resources: Expected under 250 MB output, under 128 MB per observation and a few minutes native/analysis at one worker. Host/backing have >230 GB free and about 13 GB available RAM; acquire.py rechecks capacity each attempt.
